children.text: kālatrayākhilajināṃśca tadīyadharmān saṅghān mahādaratayā praṇipatya cāpi /
children.translated_text: Having prostrated with great reverence to all the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) of the three times, to their <s>Dharma</s>, and to the <s>Saṅghas</s>,

children.text: bodhiprabheṇa kathito viśadīkaromi śiṣyottamena khalu bodhipathapradipam // Bpp_1 //
children.translated_text: I shall illuminate the Lamp for the Path to Enlightenment (<s>Bodhipathapradīpa</s>), as taught by the excellent disciple <s>Bodhiprabha</s>. // <s>Bpp</s>_1 //
Persons are to be known as threefold: superior, inferior, and middling.

children.text: likhyate lakṣaṇaṃ teṣāṃ sphuṭaṃ pratyekabhedataḥ // Bpp_2 //
children.translated_text: Their characteristics are described clearly, each distinguished separately. // <s>Bpp</s>_2 //

children.text: upāyena tu kenāpi kevalaṃ saṃsṛteḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: One who, by whatever means, seeks only the happiness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence),

children.text: svasyaivārthe ya īheta jñeyaḥ so puruṣo 'dhamaḥ // Bpp_3 //
children.translated_text: striving solely for one's own benefit — that person is to be known as inferior. // <s>Bpp</s>_3 //
One who has turned away from sinful actions and is averse to the pleasures of existence,

children.text: ātmanirvāṇamātrārthī yo naro madhyamastu saḥ // Bpp_4 //
children.translated_text: who seeks only one's own <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation) — that person is the middling. // <s>Bpp</s>_4 //
One who, through the sufferings present in one's own continuum, desires the complete destruction

children.text: sarvasya yaḥ kṣayaṃ kāṅkṣeduttamaḥ puruṣastu saḥ // Bpp_5 //
children.translated_text: of all suffering of others in every way — that person is the superior. // <s>Bpp</s>_5 //
For those supreme beings who desire the excellent <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment),
we shall explain the proper methods taught to them by the teachers. // <s>Bpp</s>_6 //
In the presence of images of the fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>, <s>stūpas</s>, and the true <s>Dharma</s>,
one should make excellent offerings with flowers, incense, and whatever substances are available. // <s>Bpp</s>_7 //
Also the sevenfold offering taught in the <s>Samantabhadracaryā</s> (Conduct of Samantabhadra),
with an irreversible mind, up to the essence of enlightenment. // <s>Bpp</s>_8 //
With deep faith in the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), placing both knees on the ground,

children.text: bhūtvā kṛtāñjaliścāpi triścādau śaraṇaṃ vrajet // Bpp_9 //
children.translated_text: with palms joined together, one should first go for refuge three times. // <s>Bpp</s>_9 //
Then, with a mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) directed toward all beings,
seeing birth in the three unfortunate destinies (<s>durgati</s>), death, transmigration, and other [sufferings], // <s>Bpp</s>_10 //
beholding the entire suffering of the world without remainder, and from suffering and from the suffering,
and from the cause of suffering — with the desire to liberate all beings — // <s>Bpp</s>_11 //
one should generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of enlightenment) with an unwavering vow.

children.text: evaṃ praṇidhicittānām utpādetu guṇāśca ye // Bpp_12 //
children.translated_text: The virtues of thus generating the mind of aspiration (<s>praṇidhicitta</s>) // <s>Bpp</s>_12 //
have been proclaimed by <s>Maitreya</s> in the <s>Gaṇḍavyūha Sūtra</s>.
From reading that sūtra or hearing from a teacher,
the infinite virtues of the mind of enlightenment (<s>sambodhicitta</s>) // <s>Bpp</s>_13 //
having understood the stability of that [mind],
one should generate that mind again and again.
The merit has been demonstrated in the <s>Vīradattaparipṛcchā Sūtra</s>. // <s>Bpp</s>_14 //
That is written here in brief, in just three verses:

children.text: bodhicittāddhi yatpuṇyaṃ tacca rupi bhavedyadi // Bpp_15 //
children.translated_text: If the merit from <s>bodhicitta</s> were to take physical form, // <s>Bpp</s>_15 //
it would fill the expanse of space and still exceed it.
If a person were to fill Buddha-fields equal in number to the sands of the Ganges // <s>Bpp</s>_16 //
with precious gems and offer them to the Lords of the World,

children.text: yaścaikaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā cittaṃ bodhāya nāmayet // Bpp_17 //
children.translated_text: and another were to simply join palms and direct the mind toward enlightenment, // <s>Bpp</s>_17 //

children.text: iyaṃ viśeṣyate pūjā yasyānto 'pi na vidyate /
children.translated_text: this [latter] offering is superior, and its extent is immeasurable.
Having generated the aspirational mind toward enlightenment, it should be cultivated through manifold efforts. // <s>Bpp</s>_18 //
For its remembrance in future lives also, the training as taught should be observed.
Without the mind of engagement (<s>prasthānacitta</s>), there is no proper growth of the aspirational vow. // <s>Bpp</s>_19 //
Therefore, one who desires the growth of the <s>sambodhisaṃvara</s> (enlightenment vow) should firmly undertake it.
Always endowed with the other vows through the sevenfold <s>prātimokṣa</s> (individual liberation), // <s>Bpp</s>_20 //
this is the fortune of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' vow, and there is no other way.
Among the sevenfold <s>prātimokṣa</s> as taught by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, // <s>Bpp</s>_21 //
the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) vow is considered the best, endowed with the glory of celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>).
According to the method stated in the chapter on discipline (<s>śīlādhyāya</s>), in the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, // <s>Bpp</s>_22 //
the vow should be taken from a good teacher, one endowed with the proper characteristics.

children.text: yaḥ saṃvaravidhau dakṣaḥ svayaṃ ca saṃvare sthitaḥ // Bpp_23 //
children.translated_text: One who is skilled in the procedure of vows and is himself established in the vow, // <s>Bpp</s>_23 //

children.text: kṛpāluḥ saṃvare śaktaḥ jñātavyaḥ sadgurustu saḥ /
children.translated_text: compassionate and capable in the vow — he is to be known as the good teacher.

children.text: tatra yatnena na prāpto guruścaitādṛśo yadi // Bpp_24 //
children.translated_text: If, despite effort, such a teacher is not found, // <s>Bpp</s>_24 //
another method for taking the vow is therefore explained.
Just as formerly by <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when he was the king <s>Ambararāja</s>, // <s>Bpp</s>_25 //
<s>bodhicitta</s> was generated — this is clearly written here,
as stated in the <s>Mañjuśrībuddhakṣetrālaṅkāra Sūtra</s>, likewise: // <s>Bpp</s>_26 //
I generate the mind toward perfect enlightenment (<s>sambodhi</s>) in the presence of the Protector.
I invite the entire world; I shall liberate them from poverty. (Bpp 27)
Ill-will pervading the mind, or envy and jealousy —

children.text: adhyāgre na kariṣyāmi bodhiṃ prāpsyāmi yāvatā // Bpp_28 //
children.translated_text: henceforth I shall not engage in [these], until I attain <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment). (Bpp 28)
I shall practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), I shall abandon sinful desires,
and I shall train after the <s>Buddhas</s> in discipline (<s>śīla</s>), vow (<s>saṃvara</s>), and restraint (<s>saṃyama</s>). (Bpp 29)
I do not aspire to attain <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment) here in haste;
I shall remain until the furthest limit [of existence] for the sake of even a single being. (Bpp 30)
I shall purify my buddha-field (<s>kṣetra</s>), immeasurable and inconceivable,

children.text: nāmadheyaṃ kariṣyāmi daśadikṣu ca viśrutam // Bpp_31 //
children.translated_text: and I shall make my name renowned in the ten directions. (Bpp 31)
I shall purify all my bodily and verbal actions completely,
and I shall purify my mental actions; I shall do nothing unwholesome. (Bpp 32)
Established in the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of enlightenment) that is the cause of purification of one's own body, speech, and mind,
one should train in the three sets of moral discipline (<s>triśīla śikṣā</s>); there should be great respect for the three sets of moral discipline. (Bpp 33)
Therefore, through the pure <s>bodhisattva</s> vow (<s>saṃvara</s>),
the accumulations for perfect enlightenment (<s>sambodhi</s>) will be completely fulfilled by diligent effort. (Bpp 34)
For the fulfillment of the accumulations whose nature is merit (<s>puṇya</s>) and wisdom (<s>jñāna</s>),
the cause, according to all the <s>Buddhas</s>, is indeed the development of the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). (Bpp 35)

children.text: pakṣavṛddhiṃ vinā pakṣī khe noḍaḍetuṃ yathā kṣamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a bird without fully grown wings is unable to fly in the sky,
so too, one lacking the power of the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) is unable to serve the welfare of beings. (Bpp 36)

children.text: abhijñasya divārātrau yāni puṇyāni santi vai /
children.translated_text: The merits that one possessing the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) [accumulates] in a single day and night,

children.text: abhijñāyāśca rāhitye naiva janmaśateṣu ca // Bpp_37 //
children.translated_text: one without the superknowledges does not [accumulate] even in a hundred lifetimes. (Bpp 37)
One who wishes to quickly fulfill the accumulations for perfect enlightenment (<s>sambodhi</s>)
should accomplish the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) through diligent effort, free from laziness. (Bpp 38)
Without the attainment of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) do not arise;

children.text: ataḥ śamathasiddhayarthaṃ yatitavyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ // Bpp_39 //
children.translated_text: therefore, one should strive again and again for the attainment of <s>śamatha</s>. (Bpp 39)
When the factors of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) are lacking, even though one cultivates [meditation] with great effort,
even in thousands of years, <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) will not be achieved. (Bpp 40)
Therefore, relying well on the factors taught in the chapter on the accumulations for <s>samādhi</s>,
one should establish the mind on any virtuous object of meditation (<s>ālambana</s>). (Bpp 41)
When the <s>yogī</s> (practitioner) has attained <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) will also be achieved;
but without the practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), the obscurations (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) are not destroyed. (Bpp 42)
Therefore, for the complete elimination of the obscurations of affliction (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>),

children.text: prajñāpāramitāṃ yogī sopāyaṃ bhāvayet sadā // Bpp_43 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> should always cultivate <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) endowed with skillful means (<s>upāya</s>). (Bpp 43)
Since wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) without skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), and skillful means without wisdom,

children.text: yato bandha iti proktau praheyaṃ nobhayaṃ tataḥ // Bpp_44 //
children.translated_text: are both declared to be bondage, therefore neither should be abandoned. (Bpp 44)

children.text: kā prajñā ka upāyaśca śaṅkāmiti nirāsitum /
children.translated_text: To dispel the doubt 'What is wisdom and what is skillful means?',

children.text: upāyasya ca prajñāyāḥ bhedaḥ samyak prakāśyate // Bpp_45 //
children.translated_text: the distinction between skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is clearly explained. (Bpp 45)
Apart from <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) and the others,

children.text: sarve hi kuśalāḥ dharmāḥ upāyāḥ jinabhāṣitāḥ // Bpp_46 //
children.translated_text: all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are declared by the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) to be skillful means (<s>upāya</s>). (Bpp 46)
One whose mind is mastered through the practice of skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) and who cultivates wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>),

children.text: śīghraṃ sa labhate bodhiṃ na nairātmyaikabhāvanāt // Bpp_47 //
children.translated_text: quickly attains <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment) — not by meditating on selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) alone. (Bpp 47)
The understanding that the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), and elements (<s>dhātu</s>) are unborn,
the knowledge of the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) — that is proclaimed as wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). (Bpp 48)
The arising of what exists is illogical, and what does not exist is like a sky-flower;
since both [positions] entail faults, neither of the two arises. (Bpp 49)
An entity is not produced from itself, nor from another, nor from both,

children.text: ahetuteśca no tasmāt niḥsvabhāvaḥ svarupataḥ // Bpp_50 //
children.translated_text: nor without a cause; therefore, it is without inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>) by its very nature. (Bpp 50)
Alternatively, when all <s>dharmas</s> are examined as one or many,
since their inherent nature is not found, there is certainty of their lack of inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>). (Bpp 51)
In the Śūnyatāsaptati (Seventy [Verses] on Emptiness), the Yukti[ṣaṣṭikā], the Mūlamadhyamaka[kārikā], and other [texts],
the established [fact] that entities are empty of inherent nature has been taught. (Bpp 52)

children.text: granthasya gauravo yasmāt atra tasmānna vistaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the text would become excessively lengthy, therefore no elaboration [is given] here;
only the established conclusions are taught for the purpose of meditation. (Bpp 53)
Therefore, the meditation on selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) — [arising] from the non-apprehension of the inherent nature of all <s>dharmas</s> whatsoever —

children.text: nairātmyabhāvanā yā hi sā prajñāyāstu bhāvanā // Bpp_54 //
children.translated_text: that is the meditation on wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). (Bpp 54)
By wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), the inherent nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is not seen;

children.text: yuktayā parīkṣya tāṃ prajñāṃ so 'vikalpena bhāvayet // Bpp_55 //
children.translated_text: having examined that wisdom by reasoning, one should cultivate it non-conceptually. (Bpp 55)
This existence (<s>bhava</s>) which has become [a realm of] conceptual elaboration (<s>vikalpa</s>), whose nature is conceptual elaboration —
For the complete abandonment of all conceptual constructions (<s>kalpa</s>) is indeed the supreme <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. [Bpp 56]

body.translated_text: Thus too it has been said by the Blessed One:

children.translated_text: Conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>) is indeed the great ignorance (<s>mahāvidyā</s>), that which causes one to fall into the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
for one established in non-conceptual <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), the non-conceptual shines forth like space. [Bpp 57]

body.translated_text: In the <s>Avikalpapraveśadhāraṇī</s> (Dhāraṇī of Entering the Non-Conceptual) too it is said:

children.translated_text: When the sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One) contemplate this non-conceptual true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: vikalpaṃ durgamaṃ tīrtvāvikalpo prāpsyate kramāt // Bpp_58 //
children.translated_text: having crossed over the difficult-to-traverse conceptual thought, the non-conceptual will be attained gradually. [Bpp 58]
Through scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and reasoning (<s>yukti</s>), having ascertained that all
<s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are devoid of inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) and unborn (<s>anutpanna</s>), one should cultivate the non-conceptual. [Bpp 59]
Meditating in this very way, having gradually attained the stages of warmth (<s>uṣṇatva</s>) and so forth,
one obtains [the stage of] Joy (<s>Pramuditā</s>) and the rest — the awakening of a <s>Buddha</s> is not far off. [Bpp 60]
Through powers of <s>mantras</s> (sacred incantations) accomplished by the practices of pacification (<s>śānti</s>), increase (<s>vistara</s>), and other ritual actions,
and through the power of the eight great <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural accomplishments) such as the <s>bhadrakumbha</s> (auspicious vase) and others, [Bpp 61]
if one desires the complete fulfillment of the accumulations for awakening (<s>bodhisambhāra</s>) with ease,
one should seek the <s>guhyācaraṇa</s> (secret conduct) initiation taught in the <s>Kriyā</s>, <s>Caryā</s>, and other <s>tantras</s>. [Bpp 62]
Then, for the purpose of receiving the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) initiation (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), through offerings of great jewels and the like,
one should please the excellent <s>guru</s> (teacher) with devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), by observing all instructions and so forth. [Bpp 63]
When the <s>guru</s> is pleased and one has received the complete <s>ācārya</s> initiation,
one whose soul is purified of all sins will become a partaker of <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments). [Bpp 64]
In the great <s>Ādibuddha Tantra</s>, it is emphatically prohibited:
the secret-wisdom initiation (<s>guhyaprajñābhiṣeka</s>) should not be taken by one who observes celibacy (<s>brahmacārin</s>). [Bpp 65]
If that initiation is taken by those established in the austerity of celibacy (<s>brahmacaryatapas</s>),
since it involves prohibited conduct, there will be destruction of the austerity and the vows (<s>saṃvara</s>). [Bpp 66]
For that vow-holder, <s>pārājika</s> (defeats, the gravest transgressions) and calamities arise;

children.text: saḥ pateddurgatau nūnaṃ siddhirnaiva kadācana // Bpp_67 //
children.translated_text: he will surely fall into evil destinies (<s>durgati</s>), and <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) will never come. [Bpp 67]
One who has received the <s>ācārya</s> initiation and is a knower of reality (<s>tattvavid</s>), in listening to all <s>tantras</s>, in commentaries,
and in performing fire rituals (<s>homa</s>), worship (<s>yajña</s>), and other rites — such a one incurs no fault. [Bpp 68]
The path to awakening (<s>Bodhipatha</s>) has been expounded in brief by <s>Dīpaṅkaraśrī</s> (the glorious <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>),
having examined the <s>Dharma</s> teachings in <s>sūtras</s> and other [texts], as an offering of the light of awakening (<s>Bodhiprabha</s>). [Bpp 69]
